table_title: List the top 10 best-selling automobiles by cumulative units sold worldwide per Wikipedia 'List of best-selling automobiles' master article's 'Best-selling car nameplates of all time' table, with manufacturer headquarters country supplemented from each manufacturer's Wikipedia page. Implicit-join framing: the master table has 4 columns (Nameplate / Production / Units sold / Notes — there is NO separate Manufacturer column per cycle-2 post-staging audit's source-attribution clarification); Manufacturer is DETERMINISTICALLY DERIVED from each Nameplate cell's leading manufacturer-prefix token (Toyota Corolla → Toyota; Ford F-Series → Ford; Volkswagen Golf → Volkswagen; Honda Civic → Honda); the HQ Country cell requires an implicit join to each derived manufacturer's Wikipedia page (Toyota / Ford Motor Company / Volkswagen / Honda — 4 unique manufacturers across the 10-row universe). NOT framed as an independently authoritative global ranking — per the Wikipedia master's own caveat, cumulative vehicle-sales figures have no definitive measurement standard; the staged values are 'per Wikipedia's best-selling car nameplates table' verbatim. Universe is the closed canonical 10-row top-10 by the master's Units sold column. For each top-10 nameplate, give Manufacturer (deterministically derived from master's Nameplate leading-prefix token; no separate Manufacturer column exists in the master), Cumulative Units Sold (numeric in millions, stripped from master's text 'million' suffix), Production Years (text range verbatim per master — '1966–present' for active production / '1938–2003' for discontinued models / '1976–2023' for recently discontinued like Ford Fiesta), and HQ Country (per-manufacturer Wikipedia page verbatim sovereign-state form, with Ford 'US' normalized to 'United States' per cycle-1 audit required edit #5). Master-derived 10-row dump provided verbatim by cycle-1 pre-staging audit from the Wikipedia master's 'Best-selling car nameplates of all time' table.
db_analog: WITH top_10_automobiles AS (SELECT nameplate, derive_manufacturer_from_nameplate(nameplate) AS manufacturer, units_sold_millions, production_years, master_row_position FROM best_selling_car_nameplates_master ORDER BY units_sold_millions DESC, master_row_position ASC LIMIT 10) SELECT a.nameplate AS model, a.manufacturer, a.units_sold_millions AS cumulative_units_sold_millions, a.production_years, m.hq_country FROM top_10_automobiles a INNER JOIN manufacturer_pages m ON normalize_manufacturer_identity(a.manufacturer) = normalize_manufacturer_identity(m.manufacturer_name) ORDER BY a.units_sold_millions DESC, a.master_row_position ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of best-selling automobiles' master article (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_automobiles), specifically the 'Best-selling car nameplates of all time' table, accessed via cycle-1 pre-staging audit's master-derived 10-row dump on 2026-05-20. Universe is the closed canonical 10-row top-10 by the master's Units sold column. Per cycle-1 audit's required edits: (1) instance ID + column name renamed from 'units_produced' to 'units_sold' — the master column is literally 'Units sold' NOT 'Units produced' (the distinction matters because some models have production figures that diverge from sales figures, e.g., for export-heavy or fleet-only models); (2) staged top-10 identity is the master's verbatim ranking (my pre-audit parametric estimate was wrong at ranks 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 — I had Honda Civic at 4 instead of VW Passat; Beetle at 5 instead of Civic; Ford Escort at 6 instead of Toyota Camry; Hilux at 7 instead of Ford Fiesta; Passat at 9 instead of Hilux; Chevy Impala at 10 instead of Honda Accord — Lada Classic + Chevy Impala + Ford Escort all OUT of top-10 per master's ranking); (3) source_count = 5 (1 master list + 4 unique manufacturer Wikipedia pages: Toyota, Ford Motor Company, Volkswagen, Honda — deduped per audit HYGIENE; the 10 models span only 4 unique manufacturers: Toyota×3 + Volkswagen×3 + Ford×2 + Honda×2); (4) Cumulative Units Sold (millions) staged as numeric values stripped from master's text 'million' suffix (50 not '50 million'; 21.5 not '21.5 million'); (5) Ford HQ normalization from the Ford Motor Company page's infobox 'US' to staged 'United States' per benchmark-consistent sovereign-state form (HQ Country is joined from each manufacturer's Wikipedia page, not from the master, which has no HQ column). Per the Wikipedia master's own caveat: cumulative vehicle-sales figures have no definitive measurement standard; the staged values are 'per Wikipedia's best-selling car nameplates table' verbatim — NOT an independently authoritative global ranking. Per-row cells: Model verbatim from Wikipedia master Nameplate column (e.g., 'Toyota Corolla' / 'Ford F-Series' with hyphen / 'Volkswagen Passat'); Manufacturer DETERMINISTICALLY DERIVED from the master's Nameplate column per cycle-2 post-staging audit's source-attribution clarification — the Wikipedia master's 'Best-selling car nameplates of all time' table has only 4 columns (Nameplate / Production / Units sold / Notes), NOT a separate Manufacturer column; Manufacturer is extracted as the leading manufacturer-prefix from each Nameplate cell (Toyota Corolla → Toyota; Ford F-Series → Ford; Volkswagen Golf → Volkswagen; Honda Civic → Honda) via mechanical leading-token rule — a deterministic curator-derivation that introduces no judgment beyond known manufacturer-vocabulary lookup. Staged Manufacturer values use single-word forms: 'Toyota' / 'Ford' / 'Volkswagen' / 'Honda' (NOT 'Toyota Motor Corporation' / 'Ford Motor Company' / 'Volkswagen AG' / 'Honda Motor Co.' even though per-manufacturer Wikipedia pages use the longer corporate forms; manufacturer-identity normalization happens at db_analog join via `normalize_manufacturer_identity()` per cycle-2 PulitzerTonyPlays precedent); Cumulative Units Sold (millions) numeric in millions (50 / 43 / 37 / 34 / 28 / 22 / 22 / 21.5 / 21 / 19.5 — rank-6 and rank-7 tied at 22 preserved per master's source-table-row-order: Toyota Camry before Ford Fiesta per Wikipedia master's verbatim sequence; CSV order is source-faithful, NOT alphabetic Model ASC — per cycle-2 post-staging audit's tiebreak-prose clarification); Production Years text-range verbatim per master with en-dash separator + 'present' marker for active production ('1966–present' / '1948–present' / '1974–present' / '1973–present' / '1972–present' / '1982–present' / '1976–2023' Ford Fiesta recently discontinued / '1938–2003' Volkswagen Beetle classic discontinued / '1968–present' / '1976–present'); HQ Country per-manufacturer Wikipedia page verbatim sovereign-state form ('Japan' for Toyota + Honda; 'United States' for Ford [joined from the Ford Motor Company page's infobox 'US', normalized per audit edit #5]; 'Germany' for Volkswagen). Implicit-join framing: the master ranks Nameplates (Models) by Units sold and gives Production Years; Manufacturer is deterministically derived from each Nameplate's leading token (the master has only Nameplate/Production/Units sold/Notes — no separate Manufacturer column); HQ Country requires an implicit join from each derived manufacturer to its Wikipedia page (4 unique manufacturer pages joined to 10 model rows). db_analog explicitly models this INNER JOIN on normalize_manufacturer_identity() (per cycle-2 PulitzerTonyPlays precedent — raw-label join would miss-match Wikipedia-master 'Volkswagen' vs per-manufacturer-page 'Volkswagen AG' / 'Ford' vs 'Ford Motor Company' label-form differences). temporal_sensitivity = low — lifetime-cumulative units sold figures shift slowly; only active-production rows (Corolla / F-Series / Golf / Passat / Civic / Camry / Hilux / Accord) increment annually; discontinued rows (Ford Fiesta 2023 / VW Beetle 2003) are stable. Sort: Cumulative Units Sold DESC primary + master-source-table-row-order ASC tiebreak (resolves rank-6/rank-7 tie at 22M units — master's verbatim table presents Toyota Camry before Ford Fiesta; CSV preserves this source-faithful order per cycle-2 post-staging audit's tiebreak-prose clarification, NOT alphabetic Model ASC which would put Ford Fiesta first).
